summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 1.16/829)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Afandəm kul yawme d ḥəššabo hawyowa qaʕide, mawṣewolle baʕ ʕitawoṯo, kul ḥa, kul yawme d ḥəššabo qəm du baytayḏe gəd konəš, maǧburi. Laǧan i mamlake d lə nətno, d lə ḥərwo w d lə milawto. Kul ənsan qəm du baytayḏe maǧburi kunašwo.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: Sir, every Sunday there would be a rule; they had given instructions in the churches, everyone, every Sunday he should sweep in front of his house, obligatorily. So that the country should not stink, should not deteriorate and should not become dirty. Every person was obliged to sweep in front of his house.

rationale: First Infectum example; dependent negative feminine predicate. English: supplied project machine translation.

data.turoyo: Ḥzele a tre tartemeniye klen miṯe, koṯe reḥo pis menayye, natini.
data.translation: Dort sah er die beiden Unholde todt liegen; ein hässlicher Geruch ging von ihnen aus, sie waren in Verwesung.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell; plural state bearers and an overt bad-smell clause support stinking, without inventing a decay sense from German.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part act. (Jan 2.35/5652)

data.translation: Where did this stinking aversion come to us from?

rationale: Second Part act. example; feminine demonstrative form and abstract head. English: supplied project machine translation.

summary: All three occurrences retain the established stinken sense. Preterit Intransitive natən/natini describes an ambient or bodily state, while natino is an adjective-like Part act. predicate in a relative clause.
The market is a non-agentive state bearer, with mu reḥo da qṭile as cause/source. The two dead giants are plural state bearers; koṯe reḥo pis menayye explicitly supports the smell reading.
German waren in Verwesung names the condition associated with the smell at PrS 33/55; it does not establish a separate lexical rot/decompose sense.
The inherited market quotation and the straw quotation are not repeated. PrS 19/29 versus prs 47/10 remains a numbering-concordance question.

Second round, Jan Beṯ-Şawoce. English quotations are the supplied project machine translation, not an edition translation; semantic decisions are based on the Turoyo. Earlier-round proposals are inherited for context only and are not repeated in this JSON.
nətno after d lə in a purpose clause is finite feminine Infectum, parallel to the other dependent predicates, distinct from inherited adjectival natino.
The stinking-aversion adjective adds a feminine demonstrative surface form; it does not establish a separate finite repellent meaning or fixed idiom.
Verify whether inherited prs 47/10 and supplied PrS 19/29 are alternative edition references for the same market quotation before changing the citation.
Confirm natəntaṯe segmentation and the force of qarafe in Jan 2.35/5652; is the stench image conventional or an individual evaluation?
Restore the adjective ending: hässlich → hässliche
rationale: The adjective modifying feminine nominative Stute after eine requires -e. The supplied edition translation repeats the missing ending, but it is an evident German typo.

summary: natəntaṯe modifies abstract qarafe with an evaluative stench image; a figurative participant extension, not a new numbered sense.
